sn12.33:1.2: “Grounds for knowledge” (_ñāṇavatthu_) are those things whose understanding leads to liberation.
sn12.33:5.1: _Dhamme ñāṇaṁ_ is the knowledge of what is visible in the present life (cf. _diṭṭheva dhamme_). It contrasts with _anvaye ñāṇaṁ_, knowledge inferred to the past and future. The two, along with knowledge of others’ minds and conventional knowledge, are also at [dn33:1.11.103](), [dn34:1.5.35](), [vb16:307.1]().
sn12.33:5.2: The same phrase is found in [sn42.11:2.9](), which also discusses what is presently observable and what is inferred. Similar terms also describe one who realizes the Dhamma as a stream-enterer ([mn56:18.8]()).
sn12.33:7.2: This knowledge “inferred” from the principles of the teaching allows Sāriputta to state that there has never been, nor ever will be, anyone more enlightened than the Buddha, even though he cannot read all the Buddhas’ minds ([sn47.12:6.2](), [dn16:1.17.8]() and [dn28:2.2]()). Pasenadi similarly is able to “infer from the teaching” that the Buddha is awakened from his behavior; this shows that this is not a special faculty of awakening, for Pasenadi was not enlightened ([mn89:13.17]()). Nonetheless, a fool like Sunakkhatta cannot infer in this way ([mn12:5.1]()).
